::: {#sol-pairs}

The strings $\mathtt{abab}$ and $\mathtt{bbab}$ pass: each of their $\mathtt{a}$s has a $\mathtt{b}$ right after it.
The empty string $\lambda$ passes too, since it has no $\mathtt{a}$ that could fail.
The string $\mathtt{aab}$ fails, because its first $\mathtt{a}$ is followed by an $\mathtt{a}$,
and $\mathtt{ba}$ fails, because its $\mathtt{a}$ is followed by nothing.

To check a string from left to right, the program only has to remember one of three things about what it has read so far:
that every $\mathtt{a}$ so far has its $\mathtt{b}$,
that the last symbol was an $\mathtt{a}$ still waiting for its $\mathtt{b}$,
or that the check has already failed.

:::
